summary: This paper experimentally and theoretically investigates how bipartite entanglement between mode pairs degrades in a Josephson parametric amplifier (JPA) when the number of parametric pump tones is increased from one to fifteen. The work demonstrates that additional pumps redistribute two-mode squeezing correlations across a larger network of modes and idler frequencies, reducing the logarithmic negativity of any individual mode pair despite constant or increasing total pump power.
motivation: Cluster states in microwave parametric circuits are a resource for continuous-variable quantum computing, but achieving high-quality multimode entanglement in superconducting systems requires understanding how multiple pumps couple modes. The fundamental trade-off between network connectivity and usable bipartite entanglement in microwave platforms remains unclear.
method: The authors pumped a SNAIL-based JPA (resonance frequency $5.808$ GHz, quality factor $Q \approx 500$) with frequency combs containing up to 15 pump tones spaced by $0.1$ MHz, measuring quadrature correlations via heterodyne detection with a Presto arbitrary waveform generator. Theory was developed using conditional Gaussian dynamics (Riccati equations) with measured cavity parameters $\kappa/2\pi \approx 6$ MHz and $\gamma = 0.21\kappa$, accounting for measurement backaction and losses via an attenuator channel.
result: Logarithmic negativity $E_N$ between the central mode pair $(-1, 1)$ dropped rapidly with increasing pump number in both symmetric and asymmetric configurations, from $E_N \sim 0.5$ (single pump) to near zero with 15 pumps, with decay independent of whether the Hilbert space size remained fixed (symmetric) or grew via extra idler modes (asymmetric), indicating redistribution rather than dilution drives the entanglement loss.
